website_scan.current_strength: The site has strong proof content: Projects, Reports, Learn, Questions, public catalogs, benchmark numbers, and limitations.
website_scan.main_gap: The central question is how to make the proof more explorable. A modern technical portfolio should let a visitor interact with a demo, inspect a system map, and see visual proof in the first minute.
website_scan.distance_from_modern_standard: Medium. The foundation is credible and content-rich, but it needs an interactive proof demo, 3D system map, richer charts, and a clearer preview path before it feels like a 2026 AI engineering surface.
next_ui_moves: Create an interactive proof tour that walks through AML Engine, Agent Chess, Heartbeat Lab, Reports, and Questions.
Create a 3D or spatial system map where proof lanes are nodes and evidence links are edges.
Add chart PNG and PDF exports from the report catalog.
Add a local preview guard so file preview does not look broken when root assets are not loaded.
Keep 3D functional: use it to explain system structure, not just as decoration.
Add a stack radar that teaches current AI engineering layers and maps each layer to a proof surface.

modern_questions.question: How do you make an AI answer with sources instead of just sounding confident?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: Teams want AI systems that can point back to the file, article, transaction, or report behind an answer.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Use Bionic Banker articles as a public corpus, retrieve relevant chunks, cite the source, and score the answer quality.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: Read the RAG, embeddings, audit log, and observability definitions, then follow the Proof Tour evidence route.

modern_questions.question: When is vector search better than keyword search?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: Search gets harder when the visitor asks in different words than the article used.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Compare article retrieval by exact keywords against embedding-based retrieval on the same public content.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: Look for whether the retrieved source actually answers the question, not only whether it contains similar words.

modern_questions.question: How do you know an AI workflow improved instead of just changed?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: A model can feel better while becoming less reliable on edge cases.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Turn glossary answers, RAG answers, and AML explanations into small pass/fail eval rows with notes.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: The Reports page shows the shape of the measurement layer and the limits attached to each number.

modern_questions.question: What should an AI agent be allowed to do by itself?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: Finance, healthcare, and compliance workflows need role boundaries, approval gates, and reviewable actions.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Map agent actions into viewer, reviewer, operator, and admin roles, then log what each role can and cannot do.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: Follow the RBAC, audit log, tool calling, and MCP concepts as one governance pattern.

modern_questions.question: Can a technical portfolio explain itself before the first call?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: Recruiters, customers, and collaborators usually need a fast path from claim to proof.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Use a guided Proof Tour with scenes, evidence rows, limits, source links, and next questions.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: Open Proof Tour and move through AML, agents, heartbeat, governance, and stack signals.

modern_questions.question: Can a system map show how projects connect without exposing private infrastructure?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: Complex agent systems are easier to understand when the relationships are visible.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Represent projects, reports, learning concepts, and public proof links as connected nodes.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: The current Proof Tour map is the first flat version. A richer spatial map can come next.

modern_questions.question: What turns a local AI demo into something reliable enough to run again?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: A demo becomes stronger when it can be packaged, health-checked, monitored, and redeployed.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Use Docker and Kubernetes as proof of packaging, service health, and predictable deployment.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: Start with the deployment reliability card in the Modern AI Stack Radar.

modern_questions.question: What does a clean API boundary look like for an AI proof system?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: Agents, frontends, and reports need stable contracts instead of loose files everywhere.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Wrap public-safe catalogs with schema validation, simple endpoints, and tests.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: Compare the catalog pages today with the future API route once it exists.

modern_questions.question: What makes an AI project feel like engineering evidence, not a blog claim?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: Technical reviewers want methods, numbers, source links, limitations, and repeatable artifacts.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Turn proof catalogs into report cards, charts, method notes, and public-safe appendices.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: Open Reports and check whether each number has context and limits.

modern_questions.question: Can one research artifact become a blog, carousel, thread, and README without losing accuracy?
modern_questions.why_people_ask: Good technical work often stays invisible because every platform needs a different shape.
modern_questions.how_we_are_testing: Draft platform-specific packets from the same public-safe source catalog.
modern_questions.what_reader_can_check: The Learn page explains the concept layer that future posts can reuse.

gaps.why_market_wants_it: AI teams need systems that retrieve source material, reduce guessing, and show where answers came from.
gaps.proof_we_have: Learning layer explains RAG. Agent Framework Proof v2 includes vector retrieval and citation-shaped proof.
gaps.proof_missing: Public demo showing ingestion, chunking, retrieval, answer generation, citations, and eval score on a small public dataset.
gaps.build_quest: Build a public RAG mini-lab using Bionic Banker articles as the corpus and show retrieval traces.

gaps.why_market_wants_it: RAG and agent memory depend on embeddings, indexing, retrieval speed, and source matching.
gaps.proof_we_have: Concept definition exists. Local agent proof mentions vector retrieval.
gaps.proof_missing: Public comparison of FAISS or Chroma retrieval against keyword search on the same article corpus.
gaps.build_quest: Create a small vector search proof with 20 to 50 public article chunks and a report chart for retrieval hit quality.

gaps.why_market_wants_it: Agent teams need to know what changed, what failed, and whether quality is improving.
gaps.proof_we_have: Agent Framework Proof v2 has test counts. Reports page shows public metrics. Heartbeat Lab shows observable loop status.
gaps.proof_missing: Public eval dashboard with pass/fail cases, judge notes, regression trend, and failure taxonomy.
gaps.build_quest: Add an eval mini-dashboard that scores glossary answers, RAG answers, and AML explanations against expected criteria.

gaps.why_market_wants_it: Modern buyers and recruiters want to inspect value quickly instead of only reading claims.

gaps.why_market_wants_it: Interactive 3D and spatial views are useful when they reveal structure, relationships, and system motion.
